title: Cyrus and the Deadline
premise: Coral Dravenmoor, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives calls on a burner phone that shouldn't exist — from their own voice, three years younger, recorded before the leak that scattered their life. The voice is a dead-man's switch built by a murdered colleague, and it begins broadcasting fragments of proof that three governments buried a market-manipulation scheme tied to an assassin's paymaster. Hunted across borders by the assassin Vess and betrayed by the handler who once protected them, Coral must smuggle the archive to Frankfurt before markets open. In the end Coral trades their own anonymity for the truth: the data goes public, Vess is exposed by her own employer, and Coral loses every name but gains, for the first time, one that belongs to them.
about_author: K. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former financial-compliance analyst who left the industry after testifying in two closed-door inquiries. They write thrillers from a coastal town whose location they decline to confirm.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Coral, living quietly in Rotterdam as 'Mara Voss', follows their rigid safety rituals until a burner phone arrives in the mail with no sender. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — the rules are working, so why does the phone feel like a summons?

chapters.title: A Voice You Buried
chapters.summary: The phone rings; the caller is Coral's own voice, recorded years earlier, reciting coordinates and a countdown to the Frankfurt open. Coral recognizes the cadence of their dead colleague Ilya's editing software. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into dread.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Coral's old handler, Brandt, warns them the safe-house protocol changed overnight — someone inside leaked their Rotterdam address. Coral flees with only the phone. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: betrayal; the system meant to protect them is the trap.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Introduce the assassin Vess in Berlin, reviewing a contract file with Coral's four names listed and a fifth name redacted. She works methodically, almost tenderly. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: cold competence hiding a flicker of doubt about her paymaster.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Switch
chapters.summary: Coral decodes the first fragment: Ilya built the switch before his 'accident', seeding it to activate if his death was ruled suspicious. It contains ledger pages naming officials in three governments. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Coral contacts Sefa, an investigative journalist who once burned them publicly, offering the archive in exchange for publication guarantees. Old wounds reopen. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: humiliation transformed into cautious alliance.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Crossing into Germany, Coral is flagged at a border checkpoint by a system that shouldn't know their face. They escape through a freight yard, but the phone broadcasts their route to whoever holds its twin. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: paranoia — even the lifeline is a leash.

chapters.title: The Paymaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vess traces the redacted fifth name and finds it matches her own alias — she was always meant to be the fall witness. She confronts her broker, who denies nothing. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: the professional calm beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe Hands
chapters.summary: Brandt offers Coral refuge in Brussels, but Coral finds surveillance gear freshly installed and realizes Brandt sold them upward, not out. A near-miss escape through canal tunnels. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into self-reliance.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Sefa's research confirms the scheme spans a regulator, a defense ministry, and a tax authority, all laundered through Frankfurt clearing houses. The countdown accelerates. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: awe and terror at the scale of the machine.

chapters.title: What the Voice Won't Say
chapters.summary: The recording skips over one crucial segment — Ilya deliberately withheld it, leaving a key phrase only Coral would recognize: a private joke about deadlines. Coral understands the final piece is hidden where they first met. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: tenderness inside tradecraft.

chapters.title: Train to Cologne
chapters.summary: Coral and Sefa ride a night train while Vess boards two cars back, ordered to take the archive and leave no witnesses. A silent game of recognition in the dining car. POV: alternating Coral/Vess. Emotional beat: two hunters realizing they want the same master dead.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Vess corners Coral but proposes a temporary truce: her contract lists her as expendable, and the ledger proves it. Uneasy partnership sealed with mutual leverage. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: belonging offered in the strangest place — between enemies.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: In a Cologne records annex, Coral retrieves Ilya's hidden drive using the deadline joke as the passphrase. An alarm trips silently; someone knows. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the certainty of pursuit.

chapters.title: Brandt's Confession
chapters.summary: Brandt intercepts them, half-apologizing, half-threatening, revealing he rewrote Coral's protocols for years to keep them controllable. Coral walks away rather than kill him. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: refusing corruption even when justice outside the law tempts it.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Before Dawn
chapters.summary: The team scatters decoys across the city while Coral carries the drive toward the exchange district, minutes from market open. Vess draws off the strike team. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: breathless momentum, every street a decision.

chapters.title: Open
chapters.summary: As the bell rings, Sefa publishes the archive live; screens across Europe flicker with the ledger. Markets convulse; ministers resign by lunchtime. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: catharsis — the truth gets past everyone at once.

chapters.title: Vess Unbound
chapters.summary: Her paymaster orders Vess eliminated as a loose end; she survives the ambush because Coral warned her, repaying the truce. She disappears into the city, free and unmoored. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: liberation that feels like exile.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Coral learns the redacted fifth name on Vess's contract was never theirs — it was a placeholder for whoever survived longest. The hunt was designed to produce a scapegoat, not a corpse. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: cold clarity about how power spends people.

chapters.title: Testimony Without a Witness
chapters.summary: Parliamentary inquiries begin; Coral could testify under protection and reclaim a legal identity, but it means re-entering the system that failed them. They choose to stay outside it, feeding evidence instead. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: choosing principle over comfort.

chapters.title: One Name That Belongs
chapters.summary: On Ilya's grave, Coral burns the four aliases' documents and speaks their original name aloud for the first time in three years. Sefa stands witness. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: mourning turned into reclamation — belonging found in being known.

chapters.title: Deadline Passed
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a new burner phone arrives, ringing with a stranger's frightened voice asking for help. Coral answers. POV: Coral. Emotional beat: quiet resolve — justice outside the law now has a switchboard, and Coral is on the line.
